title: Monitor showing itself
technique: A 3D desk of found objects with a monitor whose screen displays the previous frame of the same camera, so real video feedback builds a tunnel of monitors inside monitors.
music: Kicks flash the lamp light, make the brass astrolabe glow, light up the screen and nudge the camera in, snares make the amphora jump and hi-hats rattle the gramophone and the little lander, and each of these events then travels down the tunnel as a delayed echo. Each nested copy shifts in colour, and the direction of that shift reverses when the song changes section.

takes.name: Desk at night
takes.description: A three-quarter view of the whole desk in a blue room with a warm pool of lamp light on the objects and a rainbow tunnel on the screen.
words: VIDEO FEEDBACK ON A 3D MONITOR
The monitor's screen shows the previous frame of this same camera.
Each copy inside is 4 frames older and its colours are turned a step.

takes.name: Dolly into the screen
takes.description: A head-on view of a brightly lit room with a red wall, where the camera travels into the screen and seamlessly re-emerges every two bars.
words: DROSTE ZOOM FROM REAL FEEDBACK
The screen shows the last frame of a wide camera facing it.
A second camera flies into it every 2 bars and comes out where it began.

takes.name: Spiral twist
takes.description: The head-on picture is bent into a continuously zooming spiral in which the nested monitors wind around the centre, lit in amber and blue.
words: ESCHER SPIRAL OF A FEEDBACK TUNNEL
A shader bends the monitor-in-monitor picture round its centre,
so the nested screens join into one spiral. It zooms in a level every 4 bars.

takes.name: One-bit negative
takes.description: A closer view from the left in pure black and white, where each nested copy inverts the one before it and every kick flips the whole frame.
words: ONE-BIT FEEDBACK, NEGATIVE AT EVERY LEVEL
The screen shows this camera's previous frame as a negative,
so each copy inverts the one outside it. Every kick drum swaps black and white.

takes.name: Wall of monitors
takes.description: The desk is gone and fifteen stacked monitors, lit in salmon and blue, all show the same view of the wall, with the colours jumping on kicks.
words: ONE FEEDBACK LOOP ON 15 SCREENS
Every monitor shows the previous frame of this same camera,
so the wall is filled with pictures of itself. Kick drums shift the colours.

takes.name: Terminal
takes.description: A close view of a dark green screen where a short message types itself out and repeats down the nested copies a few frames apart.
words: THIS SCREEN SHOWS ITSELF. THE CAMERA'S LAST FRAME IS THE PICTURE ON THE GLASS. EACH COPY INSIDE IS 8 FRAMES OLDER.
THE TUNNEL IS NOT DRAWN. IT IS ONE 3D RENDER, FED BACK TO ITS OWN SCREEN ONCE EVERY FRAME.
THIS TEXT IS TYPED ON THE OUTER SCREEN ONLY. THE COPIES INSIDE ARE ITS ECHOES, 8 FRAMES APART.
ONE SHADER STEP PER COPY: GREEN TINT, SCANLINES, A LITTLE LESS LIGHT. EACH COPY GETS IT AGAIN.
KICK DRUMS LIGHT THE GLASS. THE CAMERA SEES THE FLASH. ONE STEP LATER THE NEXT COPY SHOWS IT, AND SO ON.
BUILT IN TOUCHDESIGNER: RENDER TOP, FEEDBACK TOP, CACHE TOP, ONE GLSL SHADER, A MATERIAL ON THE GLASS.

takes.name: Spiral tunnel
takes.description: The screen fills most of the frame and each nested copy is turned a little more, with extra turn from the bass, making a twisting corridor of monitor frames in pink and blue.
words: FEEDBACK WITH A TURN
The screen shows this camera's previous frame, turned up to 17 degrees,
so the nested monitors wind into a tunnel. Bass notes add more turn.

takes.name: Phosphor macro
takes.description: An extreme close-up of the screen itself, broken into red, green and blue stripes and slowly panning, with the nested monitor only just readable.
words: PHOSPHOR MACRO OF THE FEEDBACK SCREEN
No camera here: this is the picture on the monitor's glass, enlarged,
and a shader splits it into red, green and blue phosphor slots.

takes.name: Words out
takes.description: There is no room, only the feedback loop running outward, so a short amber phrase drawn in the centre on each beat flies toward the viewer while changing colour.
words: VIDEO FEEDBACK
A SCREEN
SHOWING
ITS OWN LAST FRAME
CAMERA TOO CLOSE
SO EACH COPY IS
BIGGER
NOT SMALLER
WORDS FLY OUT
ONE WORD PER BEAT
DRAWN SMALL
IN THE CENTRE
HUE TURNS EACH STEP
OLDER IS BIGGER
NO ROOM
ONLY THE LOOP

as_processor: Puts the picture inside a real video feedback loop on an old monitor: it becomes the backdrop behind the desk or the image on the monitor's screen, and the loop repeats it as smaller, older, colour-shifted copies nested inside each other (spiralled, turned, 1-bit, in green phosphor, or flying outward, depending on the take).
